Mission Local’s data takeaways included:

- About 412,000 people voted, 38,000 fewer than in 2020, although the number of registered voters was about the same.
- Proposition H shifted some races from odd-year elections, when fewer people vote, to even years, when turnout is higher.
- A citywide measure passed 55–45, a 35,600-vote difference.
- A measure backed by substantial fundraising was rejected by a 13 percent margin, or 48,887 votes.
- Redistricting changed the electorates in Districts 5 and 7, likely hurting Dean Preston and benefiting Myrna Melgar; in new precincts, 52 percent of first-choice votes went to Philhour.
